guidance_note: When a fix adds a process-lifetime resource hold ('deliberately never release'), pin the handle against GC and release it on every path where the obligation ends. This fix did neither, and that produced F18, F19, F21, F24 and F32-F37.

evidence: F2's fix in 7464491 routed a squatter to FAILED only inside HoldMirrorBeacon, but ProbeMirrorBeacon still returned alive=true on any exclusive contention, so with a marker present claimMirrorPending returned pendingCovered and HoldMirrorBeacon never ran. The squatter path stayed silent.

The agent conceded 'B's transient probe backing C's covered verdict is a microsecond promise with no obligated holder'.
Duplicate of F7: the same changelog sentence names workspace_busy, which F2's fix made false, and one rewrite closed both threads.
F4's fix renamed the slot to 'snapshot producer beacon' only in filelock.go, and the changelog's copy of the same order list kept the bare 'beacon'.
guidance_note: When fixing an ambiguous name in a declared list, grep for every restatement of that list (CHANGELOG included) and fix them in one commit.

The agent's replacement wording ('each hold ... from claim through push') was itself wrong (F28).

evidence: The changelog's 'kernel proof the covering mirror is still coming' contradicted F3's revised probe contract. The reviewer also named 'The same overstatement appears at line 30's provably still coming', which the fix did not touch (F27).
guidance_note: When a finding names a second location, fix and check off both before replying 'Fixed'.

evidence: The doc's 'the burst's final mutation is always covered' is false in the probe-probe/failed-spawn arm F10 established, which F3's doc-only fix left unaddressed in user-facing docs.

F9's fix in 8762150 made ProbeMirrorBeacon a non-atomic exclusive-then-shared two-step. A shared step succeeds on a free file, so a holder dying between the steps yields BeaconAnswered and pendingCovered with no answerer, which the single exclusive probe could not produce.
guidance_note: When splitting one lock probe into several, write the interleaving table (holder appears / vanishes between each step) and check that every row lands on the safe verdict before shipping.

evidence: F8's fix made claimants hold the beacon shared, so BeaconAnswered can come from a claimant with no mirror yet, while pendingCovered's type comment still said 'a live mirror holds the beacon'.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new kind of holder, update the doc of every verdict or type that names who the holders are.

evidence: F8's fix took the claimant's hold in ensureMirrorCoverage after claimMirrorPending returned, contradicting its own reply ('the moment it owns a claim'). A racer in that gap probes unheld and spawns.
guidance_note: When a fix promises 'held from the moment X', mint the hold inside the function that establishes X, not in its caller.

evidence: The 8762150 two-step probe's comment claimed every race lands 'never on a silent covered', which is false when holder H vanishes between steps. The agent conceded and reordered (shared first, exclusive deciding last) so a vanished holder yields BeaconUnheld.
guidance_note: Do not write an absolutist race claim ('never') in a comment until each interleaving row has been checked.

evidence: Same gap as F19: the shared hold was acquired after claimMirrorPending returned. The agent adopted 'mint inside claimMirrorPending on every claimed return' with the release carried in the outcome.

A shared-step success proves only 'not exclusively held now', so a SIGKILL between the steps produced a silent BeaconAnswered under F9's two-step design. The reorder makes the exclusive attempt decide last.

A transient exclusive holder releasing between F9's two steps made the shared step succeed and read answered, so the three-state verdict did not deliver the 'obstructed never covered' property F9 and F10 were answered with.

F8's fix kept the claimant hold to process exit even on the remote-less and spawn-failure paths that call releaseClaim, so a no-longer-obligated claimant read as an answerer for later markers and defeated next-claim residue recovery that worked before. The agent tied hold release to releaseClaim.
guidance_note: When a hold stands for an obligation, give it the obligation's lifetime: release it on every path that drops the obligation, not just process exit.

evidence: The eada99e reorder left the exclusive-holder-arrives-between-steps arm reading BeaconAnswered. The agent kept the mechanism (its argument that re-probing only shrinks the window holds) and took the reviewer's own third option to 'drop the no-strand wording and state this residual explicitly'. The racer's failed spawn still records a FAILED outcome, so the deferral is loud.
guidance_note: When a reorder fixes one interleaving, state in the same commit which interleaving it leaves open, so changelog wording never claims 'no strand'.

evidence: F21's fix wrote pendingClaimed's doc as 'is answering for it via the shared beacon hold minted with the claim', yet answerForClaim returns a no-op release when a squatter blocks the mint. 0348eba rewrote the doc to 'best-effort'. guidance_note: When writing a type doc guarantee for a fix, check the error branch of the call that is supposed to deliver it.

evidence: F15's reviewer text explicitly said 'The same overstatement appears at line 30's provably still coming', and F15's fix in 8762150 rewrote only the line-47 entry, leaving line 30 for this round.
guidance_note: Treat every location a finding names as part of the fix and check each off before replying 'Fixed in'.

evidence: F14's fix wrote 'the claiming command and the mirror it spawns each hold a kernel flock beacon from claim through push', but the claimant's hold ends at its exit or claim release (after F24), before the mirror pushes. Only the overlapping pair spans claim to push.
guidance_note: When replacing an overstatement in a doc, check the new sentence against each actor's actual lifetime instead of restating the intent.

evidence: F24's fix made an un-claimed claimant stop answering with its claim, but the mirror's own beacon release stayed deferred past completeMirrorWithoutAttempt and its up-to-~10s owner-notify hook, so a mirror that had cleared its claim still read as an answerer. The fix moved an idempotent stopAnswering to the head of the completion helpers.
guidance_note: After tying one holder's release to its obligation, sweep every other holder of the same lock (the mirror as well as the claimant) for the same stale-answerer gap.

evidence: False-positive flag: the comment 'A marker that disappears under the refresh was just cleared by a push attempt' appears unchanged as context in the 8762150 and eada99e diffs, so it predates 0348eba. It is wrong because releaseClaim's clearMirrorPending on unspawnable paths also removes the marker with no push, and the reviewer's 'name both clearers' doc fix was the right call.
guidance_note: When writing an 'X vanished, so Y must have happened' comment, grep for every call that deletes X and name each one.

evidence: The eada99e reorder documented the between-steps exclusive-holder residual in ProbeMirrorBeacon's function doc but left BeaconAnswered's const doc saying 'no exclusive holder stood moments earlier', so the two docs for one verdict contradicted each other.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a residual to a function's contract, update the doc on the return type/constant it produces in the same edit.

evidence: The agent confirmed that Go's os.File installs a close finalizer, so the claimant hold F8's fix 'deliberately never releases' drops at the next GC once ensureMirrorCoverage returns and the release closure is unreachable. The 'held to process exit' property was never delivered, and 5749b00 pins the release in a package-level slice.
guidance_note: When a design relies on 'abandon the fd until process exit' in Go, keep the *os.File reachable (package-level pin or runtime.KeepAlive at the true lifetime end), because finalizers close unreachable files.

evidence: Duplicate of F32 on the adjacent line: the local releaseAnswer closure is the only reference to the File, and the finalizer can close it during the ~26s post-spawn tail. The same package pin fixes both.

F29's fix in 0348eba made stopAnswering the first step before owner-notify specifically to stop answering, but it kept '_ = releaseBeacon()', whose 'only noise at exit' rationale does not hold on that pre-effects path. A failed release silently left the dying mirror answering.
guidance_note: When moving an at-exit cleanup to a point where its success matters, re-examine whether its error can still be discarded.

evidence: False-positive flag: the owner-notify test helper's hand-derived DatabasePath was part of the original PR (the round-0 summary notes the PR 'updates the owner-notify test helper to supply DatabasePath'), and 0348eba did not introduce it. Duplicating the storage-dir to database-path geometry that workspace.LocationFromStorageDir owns was a real one-source-of-truth slip.
guidance_note: When a test fixture needs a path production derives, call the production deriver (workspace.LocationFromStorageDir) instead of rebuilding the join.

evidence: F24's fix introduced the claim that the abandoned claimant hold is 'truthful redundant backing for the mirror actually running', but the hold proves only that the claimant lives, so a SIGKILLed mirror reads as answered until the parent exits. The doc-only correction naming the bounded ~26s window was proportionate.
guidance_note: Describe what a lock hold proves in terms of its holder process, not the process it is meant to stand in for.

evidence: The changelog's 'kept to process exit' and 'no window in which a healthy spawn reads as dead' were undelivered because of the os.File finalizer from F8's unpinned hold. The agent fixed the mechanism rather than weakening the doc, which the reviewer offered as its first option.

narrative: The PR replaced a five-minute age-out with a flock liveness beacon, and 31 of its 37 findings were caused by earlier fixes. Three roots drove the cascade. F2's squatter-to-FAILED change was applied to the holder but not the prober (F9), and F9's two-step probe then introduced interleaving bugs (F17, F20, F22, F23). F3's doc-only 'benign by construction' resolution was false (F10) and left doc overstatements across three files (F14-F16, F27, F28). F8's 'hold to process exit' claimant hold was taken in the wrong place (F19, F21), outlived its obligation (F24, which spread to the mirror in F29), and was never pinned against Go's finalizer (F32, F33, F37). Rounds 2 and 3 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: Each fix to a concurrency protocol was shipped without an interleaving table for the new mechanism, so every round's fix produced the next round's races.

Doc and changelog restatements of the lock contract existed in at least three places (code comment, CHANGELOG lines 23/30/47, docs/dolt-remote-sync.md), and fixes repeatedly updated one copy while leaving the others, even when the finding named the other location.
Reply text promised properties ('the moment it owns a claim', 'kept to process exit') that the committed code did not implement, and the next round caught the gap each time.
